# The library's methods: what is already there to call

Every method below is declared in `com/herokuapp/theinternet/tests/core/`, with exactly these parameters.
**Call only a method you have seen declared**, here or in its class, with arguments of those types:
a call written from memory is the most common way new code fails to compile, and the suite's rules,
which read the sources, cannot see it. When you cannot run `mvn`, check every call you wrote
against this card before you say you are done, and say that the code was not compiled.

These are where to look first, not a fence. Page code (elements, actions, checks) may also call the
browser library itself when nothing here does what a story needs (a download, a drag, a wait for a
response); a story test never does. The rules read the sources: such a call fails them in a test, not in
page code.

A `PageElement` is a constant of a page's Elements enum (`HomeElements.ABOUT_LINK`); `page` is
the page object's browser session.

## UserActions

- `UserActions.click(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: Clicks it.
- `UserActions.clickOpeningNewTab(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)` returns `WebDriver`: Clicks something that opens a new tab, and returns the driver switched to it; the next page object lives there.
- `UserActions.hover(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: Points the mouse at it (a menu that opens on hover, a tooltip).
- `UserActions.type(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String text)`: Replaces what is in the field with this text.
- `UserActions.typeSecret(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String secret)`: Types a password or other secret. The step says a secret was typed, never what it was.
- `UserActions.clear(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: Empties the field.
- `UserActions.choose(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String option)`: Chooses an option of a dropdown (a select element) by its value or its visible text.
- `UserActions.attach(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String path)`: Attaches a file to a file field (input type="file"), by its path; a file field is never typed into.
- `UserActions.tick(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: Ticks a checkbox or picks a radio button.
- `UserActions.untick(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: Unticks a checkbox.
- `UserActions.setTicked(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, boolean ticked)`: Ticks or unticks: what a page's check() and uncheck() actions call.
- `UserActions.pressKey(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String key)`: Presses a key in it: "Enter", "Tab", "Escape", "ArrowDown".
- `UserActions.readText(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)` returns `String`: Reads the text a visitor sees in it, trimmed. The step says what it read.
- `UserActions.act(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, Consumer<WebElement> action)`: Does something to the element once it is visible, trying again while something covers it or the page redraws it, until the element timeout; then the last error says what was wrong. Every action above is built on it; a new one can be too.

## Checks

- `Checks.isShown(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: It is shown.
- `Checks.isNotShown(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: It is gone, or hidden.
- `Checks.allShown(WebDriver driver, String what, PageElement... elements)`: All of them are shown: one step, and the failure names the first one missing.
- `Checks.hasText(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String expected)`: It says exactly this (runs of spaces and line breaks count as one space).
- `Checks.hasValue(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String expected)`: A field holds exactly this: what was typed into it (a field has no text of its own to read); a dropdown, the option it shows, as chosen by its words (its value attribute can differ: "devops").
- `Checks.containsText(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String expected)`: Its text contains this.
- `Checks.pageShowsText(WebDriver driver, String text)`: The page shows this text somewhere a visitor can see it (any case; part of a longer text is fine).
- `Checks.hasCount(WebDriver driver, String what, By all, int expected)`: The page shows this many of them: hasCount(driver, "results", By.cssSelector("ul.results > li"), 3). Hidden ones (a mobile menu's copies) are not counted.
- `Checks.linksToEach(WebDriver driver, String what, java.util.List<String> hrefs)`: The page shows a link to each of these addresses, by its href as written: a list still leading where it led (G-125).
- `Checks.allDifferent(String what, java.util.List<String> names, java.util.List<String> values)`: Each value is its own: allDifferent("page types' titles", names, titles) names the two that share one (G-125).
- `Checks.clickChangesThePage(WebDriver driver, String label, String xpath)`: Clicks a control seen on most of the site's pages (a carousel's Next, a "More" toggle), by its XPath, and checks that the page around it changes: its region, itself, or the page's classes (G-125).
- `Checks.isEnabled(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: It is shown, and can be used (a button or field that is not disabled).
- `Checks.isDisabled(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: It is shown, and disabled.
- `Checks.isChecked(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: A checkbox or radio button is shown, and ticked.
- `Checks.isNotChecked(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: A checkbox or radio button is shown, and not ticked.
- `Checks.refusesEmpty(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)`: The browser will not send the field's form with the field as it is: it is required, empty, and its form leaves the browser's own check on. Asked of the field, never by sending: nothing leaves the browser (G-116).
- `Checks.hasAttribute(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, String name, String expected)`: Its attribute holds exactly this, as the page's HTML says it: hasAttribute(driver, HELP_LINK, "href", "/help").
- `Checks.isOnPath(WebDriver driver, String path)`: The browser is on this path of the site.
- `Checks.titleIs(WebDriver driver, String title)`: The page's title is exactly this.
- `Checks.assume(boolean met, String why)`: What the test needs is there (the data it uses, a state of the site): when it is not, the test is skipped, saying why, never failed. Name the data: Checks.assume(!policies.isEmpty(), "no policy with an amount due in policies.csv"). Not a check (SR-19): the test still checks something.

## WaitActions

- `WaitActions.seconds(long ms)` returns `String`: A wait as a person reads it: "10" (seconds), or "0.5".
- `WaitActions.elementTimeout()` returns `long`: How long a step waits for a URL, a title or an element: ELEMENT_TIMEOUT, unless shortened below.
- `WaitActions.shortenWaits(Long millis)`: For HarnessTest only: checks it makes fail on purpose fail in half a second, not ten. For this thread, until shortenWaits(null). A real test never shortens its waits.
- `WaitActions.waitForUrl(WebDriver driver, String path)` returns `boolean`: Waits for the browser to be on exactly this path of the site (query and #fragment aside).
- `WaitActions.waitForUrlShape(WebDriver driver, List<String> shapes)` returns `boolean`: Waits for a URL of one of these shapes, e.g. "/blog/*": "*" is one path segment, "{n}" a number.
- `WaitActions.stillLoading(WebDriver driver)` returns `List<String>`: What the page is still loading (frames, media, images) when its load event is late: shown with the note below, so a slow third party is named instead of failing a page that is there.
- `WaitActions.noteStillLoading(WebDriver driver, String name)`: Says that a page proven by its address, title and checks had not finished loading in time, and what held it.
- `WaitActions.waitForPageLoad(WebDriver driver)` returns `boolean`: Waits until the page and everything it loads has finished loading (document.readyState "complete").
- `WaitActions.waitForTitle(WebDriver driver, String title)` returns `boolean`: Waits for exactly this title (runs of whitespace count as one space).
- `WaitActions.waitForTitle(WebDriver driver, String startsWith, String endsWith)` returns `boolean`: Waits for a title that starts and ends like this (the page's own name goes in between).
- `WaitActions.waitForVisibilityOf(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)` returns `boolean`: Waits until the element is visible.
- `WaitActions.waitForVisibilityOf(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, long timeoutMs)` returns `boolean`: Waits up to timeoutMs until the element is visible.
- `WaitActions.waitForPresenceOf(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)` returns `boolean`: Waits until the element is in the page, visible or not.
- `WaitActions.waitForInvisibilityOf(WebDriver driver, PageElement element)` returns `boolean`: Waits until the element is gone or hidden: a spinner, an overlay, a "Loading..." message.
- `WaitActions.waitForInvisibilityOf(WebDriver driver, PageElement element, long timeoutMs)` returns `boolean`: Waits up to timeoutMs until the element is gone or hidden.
- `WaitActions.until(BooleanSupplier ready, long timeoutMs)` returns `boolean`: Waits up to timeoutMs until the condition holds, checking every tenth of a second.
- `WaitActions.samePage(String url, String expectedUrl)` returns `boolean`: True when both URLs are the same page: same site and path; query, #fragment and a final "/" aside.
- `WaitActions.fitsShapes(String url, List<String> shapes)` returns `boolean`: True when the URL's path has one of these shapes.
- `WaitActions.fitsShape(String url, String shape)` returns `boolean`: True when the URL's path has this shape: "*" is any one segment, "{n}" a number.
- `WaitActions.sameTitle(String title, String expected)` returns `boolean`: True when a page's title is the expected one, whatever the spacing (sameText).
- `WaitActions.sameText(String text, String expected)` returns `boolean`: True when both say the same, whatever the spacing: runs of whitespace count as one space.
- `WaitActions.containsText(String text, String expected)` returns `boolean`: True when the text contains the expected words, whatever the spacing.
- `WaitActions.titleFits(String title, String startsWith, String endsWith)` returns `boolean`: True when a title starts and ends as expected, with something between (a family's titles name their page: "Pikachu Pokédex entry | Dex"), whatever the spacing.

## SiteConfig

- `SiteConfig.settings()` returns `String`: The run's first line: each setting given, its value and where it came from; the rest are the code's defaults.
- `SiteConfig.baseUrl()` returns `String`: Where the site under test lives: the baseUrl setting, else the address the crawl read.
- `SiteConfig.url(String path)` returns `String`: The full URL of a path on the site under test, e.g. url("/about").
- `SiteConfig.secret(String name)` returns `String`: A secret a test needs (a password, an API key): from -Dname=... or the environment variable NAME (upper case; dots and dashes become underscores). Fails, saying how to pass it, when neither is set. Secrets never go into the code, a saved page or a log.
- `SiteConfig.value(String name, String fallback)` returns `String`: Test data that may differ between copies of the site (a product that exists on staging, say): from -Dname=... or the environment variable NAME, else the fallback.

## StepLog

- `StepLog.start()`: Starts a new test's log. BaseTest calls this before every test.
- `StepLog.step(String sentence)`: A step the test takes, as a visitor would say it: step("Type the email address").
- `StepLog.note(String remark)`: A remark that is not a step of its own, e.g. "now on the services page".
- `StepLog.steps()` returns `List<String>`: The steps so far, in order.
- `StepLog.reason(Throwable cause)` returns `String`: Why something failed, in one line: the first line of the message. Selenium adds the session, the browser's build and a link to its docs on the lines below; they say nothing about the site.
- `StepLog.way(String reason)` returns `String`: How a test failed, with what its reason names taken out (an address, a quoted text, a number): two tests that failed the same way on different pages have the same way (StopEarly). Every failure to reach the site is one way, whatever the test tried: "the site cannot be reached".
- `StepLog.runOf(String displayName)` returns `String`: One run of a parameterized test, by its display name ("[2] PokedexDetailPage loads pikachu"): "-2", so each run keeps its own evidence folder; "" for any other test.
- `StepLog.failure(Throwable cause)` returns `String`: What BaseTest prints when a test fails: the step it failed at, and why.
